newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul reform panel upholds bank ownership limit.
newsitem.headline: Seoul reform panel upholds bank ownership limit.

text.p: A financial reform panel, which had considered raising the individual shareholding limit in South Korean banks, has decided to continue the current four percent ceiling, a commission statement said on Tuesday.
The Presidential Commission for Financial Reform said it would propose expanding the ceiling to 10 percent only when banks were newly-opened or when other financial institutions shift into banking.
The panel had considered raising the ceiling to 10 percent to establish reponsible management in banks and to improve their competitiveness.
For newly-established banks, the 10 percent ceiling would be applied to the first five years and until their total assets reached one trillion won, the statement said.
The commission set the minium capital requirement for banks and insurers at 100 billion won and 30 billion won, respectively, unchanged from the current level.

But it lowered the requirement for securities houses to 30 billion won from 50 billion at present. For brokerage business only, the commission recommended lowering it to 15 billion won from 30 billion. That for futures trading was also proposed to be curtailed to 2.0 billion from 10 billion.

The commission stressed the need for transparency for new entrants into the non-banking financial industry. It proposed to allow the country's top five conglomerates to enter the life insurance business from the year 2000.
The commission will hold a meeting on Friday to put the finishing touches on the proposals to be sent to President Kim Young-sam on May 26.
The 31-member commission was set up in January after President Kim said he would push forward with reforming the country's backward financial sector.
